retirement_age.notes: State Pension age is 66 for men and women (people born before 6 April 1960). It is rising to 67 in a phased way for people born 6 April 1960 to 5 March 1961, completed by April 2028 under the Pensions Act 2014. A further rise to 68 is legislated for 2044 to 2046 but its timing is under review.

open_questions: No general election date is set: it must be held no later than 2029-08-15 and the prime minister can call it earlier. Date left null.
The monarch holds the post for life and the prime minister has no fixed term, so term_ends is null for both.
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister on 2026-07-20 (confirmed on gov.uk) succeeding Keir Starmer; his birth date comes from Wikipedia and several other biographies, not from an official page.
Population of 69,487,000 (30 June 2025 official estimate) is taken from a Wikipedia list; the ONS original was not opened. UN projection for 2025 is about 69.9 million.
Median age of 40.1 comes from database.earth, which republishes UN World Population Prospects 2024; other aggregators give 39.8 to 41.6. No ONS figure was retrieved.

State Pension age sources were commercial pension guides, not gov.uk; they agree with each other. The rise to 67 is described as starting in April or May 2026 (first affected cohort reaches the new age from 6 May 2026).
